title: Connect HubSpot to Claude for event ROI reporting
summary: Connect HubSpot to Claude to see pipeline and closed-won. For deeper insights into event ROI, you’ll want one more MCP. Find out which one inside.
body_markdown:
You just got back from a show, and leadership wants to know which deals it created, which reps drove them, and whether the booth paid for itself. So you open your HubSpot dashboards. The bar charts and line graphs tell you nothing. Then you wonder, “Is there a Claude connector for HubSpot?”


Yes, you can connect Claude to HubSpot. But no, it can’t answer your CMO’s questions. Here’s why: Connecting HubSpot to Claude lets you ask your CRM questions in plain language: deals by stage, open pipeline, closed-won revenue. The event questions are where it stalls. Which show created a deal, which rep captured it, how much the booth returned — that data needs to be in HubSpot before Claude can generate answers.


Whether you can report event ROI at all comes down to your event lead capture platform. The best ones give you[more than one way to see your event data](https://popl.co/pages/ask-popl-ai-assistant) , so the real question isn't whether Claude can read your CRM. It's whether the event ever made it into a system Claude can read.


This guide covers what the HubSpot–Claude connector answers, what an event lead capture platform adds, and when to use


[an AI assistant](https://popl.co/blogs/all/what-is-an-ai-assistant-for-event-lead-capture) versus a dashboard for event ROI reporting.


****


## How to connect HubSpot to Claude


Turning on HubSpot's native Claude connector takes only a few minutes. An admin switches it on once, and then each teammate connects it to Claude using their own HubSpot login.


1.


Enable it in HubSpot.


A Super Admin (or a user with App Marketplace permissions) connects the connector for the first time and opts your account in if you want Claude to read engagement history or create and edit records.


2.


Add it in Claude.


Go to Settings → Connectors → Browse connectors, search for HubSpot, and click Add.


3.


Sign in.


Authenticate with your HubSpot login. Claude then reads only what your own HubSpot permissions already allow.


HubSpot's


[setup guide for the Claude connector](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/integrations/set-up-and-use-the-hubspot-connector-for-claude) covers the specifics. But connecting is the easy part, and on event ROI, that's where it stops short.


## What the HubSpot–Claude connector offers for event ROI reporting


Claude can read your CRM and even create or update records right from the chat. It answers in plain language.

Can it answer?

No. The event isn't in the CRM

No. The CRM never recorded the scan


Which deals the show created vs. only touched


No. That needs event data HubSpot never held


****


The pattern is clear. The connector is strong on what's in HubSpot and blank on what happened at the event. A deal record shows the deal exists. It doesn't show the booth it started at, the rep who scanned the badge, the qualifier answers, or the capture date. There's nothing there to


[compute event ROI](https://popl.co/blogs/all/how-to-calculate-roi-on-event-lead-capture) from.


## What it takes to report event ROI in HubSpot


You can't report on event data your tools never captured. And most event tools never capture it. A rented badge scanner hands you a spreadsheet a week later with no rep attached, no event tag, no qualifier answers, and no way to tell a deal the show created from one it merely nudged along.


So the real requirement sits upstream of any dashboard or AI. To make event ROI reportable, the event has to become data in the first place: who captured the lead, where they captured it, what the lead said they needed, and when the deal closed. That means a full event lead capture platform, and the ones that make event ROI easy to report share three traits:

A

Event context syncs into the CRM, mapped to your own properties, with attribution set at the moment of capture.


-


An MCP connector.


You can move past static dashboards and ask granular questions inside an AI assistant like Claude.

## Event-sourced vs. event-influenced in HubSpot


Most event ROI questions come down to one thing: did this show create the deal, or just touch it? In attribution terms, that's the difference between event-sourced and event-influenced.


An event-sourced deal is one the show originated. The relationship started on the floor: a brand-new contact your rep met at the booth, now a deal that wouldn't exist otherwise. An event-influenced deal is one the show moved forward without starting. The contact had already seen your ads or talked to sales, stopped by the booth, and the show became one of several touches on the way to closed-won.


These map onto HubSpot's


[attribution reporting](https://popl.co/blogs/all/popl-hubspot-attribution-reporting-guide) rather than being HubSpot's own labels. HubSpot's native models are first-touch, last-touch, and multi-touch. You'd see a sourced deal through an original-source or deal-source property, or a first-touch report. You'd see an influenced deal through multi-touch attribution and the contact's interaction history.


Influenced is the view marketers reach for most, because it's where the messy reality lives. The prospect who turns up at three of your events before signing. The deal that traces back a year later to the booth where it actually started. A first-touch report alone would miss both.


This is where capture data earns its keep. Popl tags each lead with the event, the rep, and the capture date, and its CRM Insights already flag whether that person was a new lead or an existing account, so you have the raw material to tell sourced from influenced.

## Event ROI reporting FAQ


### 1. Can the HubSpot–Claude connector report event ROI on its own?


No, the HubSpot–Claude connector can't report event ROI on its own. It reads what's in HubSpot, like deals, pipeline, and closed-won revenue. Event ROI needs event context — the show, the rep, the qualifier answers — that only reaches HubSpot once a capture platform syncs it there. From there you can report it in a HubSpot dashboard, in an out-of-the-box dashboard like Popl Event Flows, or by asking an AI assistant like


Ask Popl


.


### 2. What's the difference between event-sourced and event-influenced in HubSpot?


An event-sourced deal is one the show created, where the relationship started on the floor. An event-influenced deal is one in which the show moved forward without starting it, with the booth as one of several touches on the way to closed-won. These map onto HubSpot's first-touch and multi-touch attribution reporting.


### 3. Do I need to build a HubSpot dashboard to see event ROI?


No, you don't need to build a HubSpot dashboard to see event ROI. A dashboard is worth building for the numbers you check on a schedule, but an out-of-the-box dashboard like Popl Event Flows gives you a standing view with no build, and an AI assistant like Ask Popl answers one-off questions on demand.


### 4. Why use an AI assistant instead of a dashboard for event ROI?


Use an AI assistant when the question isn't one you planned for. A dashboard shows the questions you set up in advance; an AI assistant like Ask Popl answers the ones you didn't, and lets you slice event ROI a new way every time you ask.
